objective: Make every canonical MasterBot/division independently capable as a domain-specialized model system, with evidence-backed competitiveness against current open-weight models.

scope.profile_generation: one independent model profile and training/evaluation lane per canonical MasterBot

architecture.division_model: A division-owned model system with a versioned model identity, approved open-weight base model, division-specific adapter or checkpoint, domain retrieval corpus, tools, policy, memory namespace, evaluation suite, and deployment manifest.
architecture.independence: Each division can complete its own domain tasks without requiring Buddy to solve the task; Buddy may route, delegate, compare, and coordinate but is not a hidden dependency for division acceptance.
architecture.shared_foundation: Base weights, tokenizer, inference runtime, safety infrastructure, and common adapters may be shared where licenses and compatibility permit. Division-specific adapters, retrieval indexes, tool permissions, evaluations, model cards, and release records remain separately versioned.
training_strategy: benchmark candidate open-weight base models before selection
start with prompting, retrieval, tool use, and structured workflows
use LoRA/QLoRA or other parameter-efficient tuning when evaluation shows a repeatable gap
consider continued pretraining or full fine-tuning only with rights-cleared data, approved compute, and reproducible baselines
train a foundation model from scratch only as a separately approved research program
architecture.no_fake_independence: A prompt template or renamed API endpoint alone does not qualify as an independently capable division model.

comparison_rules: compare same task, prompt, tool access, context, decoding settings, precision, and hardware class
report parameter count and active parameters for MoE models
report model weights/license and inference stack
repeat runs and report confidence intervals where applicable
separate public benchmark scores from private held-out scores
track contamination risk and benchmark version
compare cost, latency, throughput, memory, and reliability as well as accuracy
external_reference_sources: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index and methodology
Hugging Face Open LLM Leaderboard and evaluation documentation
LiveCodeBench or equivalent time-sensitive coding evaluation where applicable
SWE-bench Verified/Pro or equivalent repository task evaluation where applicable
GPQA Diamond and HLE where domain-appropriate

promotion_targets.domain_quality: candidate must exceed approved baseline and meet a pre-registered division-specific target on private held-out tasks
promotion_targets.frontier_comparison: report rank/score gap to the strongest license-compatible open-weight models on comparable evaluations; no blanket claim of frontier parity
promotion_targets.non_regression: no critical regression in general, safety, privacy, tool permissions, or reliability suites
promotion_targets.economics: meet division-specific latency, memory, throughput, and cost budgets
promotion_targets.reproducibility: independent rerun from pinned artifacts must reproduce within declared tolerance

execution.retry_policy: bounded retries; classify failures; do not loop on unchanged blockers
execution.scheduled_work: best-effort CI schedule; not a 24x7 compute guarantee
execution.resource_budget: per-division quotas and explicit user approval for paid compute

honesty_rules: A logical training lane is not a trained model.
A generated model profile is not proof of domain capability.
A contract benchmark is not a model-quality benchmark.
Do not claim competitiveness without comparable benchmark evidence.
Do not mark mastery without independent held-out evidence and sustained regression-free operation.
